topic: Types of Waves and Wave Propagation
key_concepts: A wave is a disturbance that propagates from a source.
Water waves spread outward from the point of disturbance.
Waves can set objects such as a paper boat in motion.
Force is required to set an object in motion.
Greater force in creating waves increases the movement of a floating object.
Increasing the rate of vibration changes the size of the waves.
In a transverse wave, particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave travel.
In a longitudinal wave, particles vibrate back-and-forth parallel to the direction of wave
Waves do not transport the medium or a marker such as a ribbon from its original position.
Waves can be classified as transverse, longitudinal, mechanical, and electromagnetic.
